title: Interim Sealing Standard for the Aft Lower Shell Longitudinal Skin Joints

issue.reason: Original issue of the interim sealing standard dossier.

abstract: First-standard sealing and drainage arrangement for the longitudinal skin joints of the aft lower shell, introduced after early-build aircraft showed sealant blistering and standing moisture below the aft cargo floor.

sections.reason: Aircraft from the first two production batches showed sealant blistering along the longitudinal skin joints of the aft lower shell at their first scheduled structural check. Nine aircraft out of the first forty delivered had visible blistering, and on three of them standing moisture was found in the joint land under the aft cargo floor panels. No corrosion had started at that point, but the joint sealant was clearly not doing its job in an area that collects condensate on short-sector operation with frequent cabin door openings.
sections.description: The faying-surface sealant specification for the longitudinal joints between stations C52 and C66 is changed from the general airframe grade to a higher elongation grade, and the joint is re-sealed as a fillet rather than a wet assembly alone. Three drain grommet positions are added at the low point of each joint land. The inner doubler at the joint, part number D5331120951225, is retained but is re-primed before installation, and the stringer run D5331122551549 is packed clear of the joint land so that water cannot be trapped between the two. Washers AGS334024-84 replace the previous plain items at the drain grommet positions. The revised detail is on drawings D53311217453 and D53311251048. Access is through the aft cargo compartment in zones 131 and 141 with the cargo floor panels lifted locally.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 0.8 kg per aircraft, symmetric, with no measurable centre-of-gravity effect. No electrical load change. The change is fully interchangeable in both directions because no fastener pattern is altered. The scheduled detailed visual inspection of the joint land is retained at the original interval. Illustrated parts content for the aft lower shell requires a sealant note rather than a part list change, and the structural repair content is unaffected.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN C00148 in January 2017. Retrofit for the earlier aircraft is offered through Service Bulletin CRN-53-1008, which is open to the whole pre-cut-in population and is expected to run for three seasons alongside the scheduled structural checks.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00148, absorbed in the aft fuselage join sequence

title: Interim Sealing Standard for the Aft Lower Shell Longitudinal Skin Joints

issue.reason: Declared superseded by the corrosion-resistant doubler standard, with the supersession and the reason for it carried on this dossier rather than only on the bulletin.

abstract: Superseded first-standard sealing and drainage arrangement for the longitudinal skin joints of the aft lower shell, introduced after early-build aircraft showed sealant blistering and standing moisture below the aft cargo floor.

sections.reason: Aircraft from the first two production batches showed sealant blistering along the longitudinal skin joints of the aft lower shell at their first scheduled structural check. Illustrated parts content for the aft lower shell requires a sealant note rather than a part list change, and the structural repair content is unaffected. This arrangement keeps water out of the joint; the standard that replaces it lets water out of the joint, and the two assumptions cannot both be held on one airframe, which is why no aircraft may carry the two arrangements in the same joint.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN C00148 in January 2017 and superseded on 16 April 2019 by MOD-111020, which addresses the same failure mode at the same joint with the same fastener by means of a titanium doubler and an open drain path. The supersession is stated here and on the superseding dossier so that neither can be read on its own. Retrofit was offered through Service Bulletin CRN-53-1008, which is cancelled; the remaining pre-cut-in aircraft are taken to the doubler standard directly.
